title: Introduce rolling stability prober and traffic cushioning policy
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Rollout guards and canaries reduce customer impact but still suffer from noisy signals when traffic is bursty or when regressions are small but persistent. This PR adds a lightweight rolling stability prober that continuously evaluates short- and medium-window signal coherence (latency/throughput/error-rate) and an accompanying traffic cushioning policy that applies a graded, reversible traffic dampening layer instead of immediate rollbacks. Design: (1) Rolling stability prober: a pluggable probe that computes multi-horizon metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, QPS, error-rate) across overlapping rolling windows and produces a stability score using entropy-weighted fusion. The prober exposes per-route scores and confidence estimators for downstream policies. (2) Traffic cushioning policy: a policy controller that consumes prober scores and applies soft controls — token-based ingress buffering, prioritized traffic classes, and temporary backpressure knobs — to reduce the rate of new work hitting hot replicas while preserving capacity for high-priority requests. The policy is stageable (observe -> cushion -> escalate) and automatically retires cushions on recovery. Implementation notes: - Prober implemented in perf-canary/probers/rolling_prober.py with a streaming aggregator and an async evaluation loop. - Policy controller implemented in runtime/routing/traffic_cushion_controller.go and integrates with the existing rollout controller via a new Policy API. - Observability: added dashboards and tracing spans (observability/dashboards/stability-prober.json) and new metrics (stability_score, cushion_level, cushion_duration_seconds). - Safety: cushions are capped by per-tenant SLAs and honor dedicated capacity reservations. Cushion actions are reversible and logged in audit events. - Tests: unit and integration tests added (tests/integration/test_stability_prober.py). Benchmarks: internal canary on a mix of synthetic and production-like workloads showed a 60% reduction in premature rollbacks and a 25% reduction in user-facing error spikes during transient regressions. Backward compatibility: Policy defaults to disabled; cluster operators must opt-in by setting enable_stability_prober=true in helm values. See docs/observability/perf-probes.md for config and runbook. The description below lists the checklist, commits, and small operational notes.

review_conversation: Diego Ruiz (2026-02-15): Left a couple of questions on confidence calibration. How do we prevent the prober from being overly sensitive when traffic distribution shifts?

Maya Chen (2026-02-15): Answered — the prober uses a weighted baseline that decays with a half-life and a stability confidence metric derived from sample-count-aware entropy; added more comments and a unit test for distribution shift in rolling_prober.py
Priya Natarajan (2026-02-17): Asked for limits on cushion ripple across tenants. Suggested adding SLA caps and explicit override for enterprise tenants.
Maya Chen (2026-02-17): Implemented SLA caps and added honor_dedicated_capacity flag. Updated helm values and docs.
Liam O'Connor (2026-02-18): Noted that audits need to capture cushion decisions for postmortems. Requested audit logs and trace linking.
Maya Chen (2026-02-19): Added audit events and trace context propagation; ran a smoke canary and attached results to the PR.
